5. Mr. Latifur Rahman, learned Counsel appearing for the appellant, has contended that under section 35(1) of the Income Tax Act the Income-tax Act Officer can rectify any mistake apparent from the record of the order of assessment within 4 years from the date of the order and that the original order of assessment for the assessment year 1949-50 having been made by the Income-tax Officer on 31-5-54 the said officer acted illegally in having rectified the alleged mistake under the aforesaid provisions of the Act on 15-7-61 which was long beyond the statutory period of 4 years and that the learned Judges of the High Court committed a substantial error in holding that the original order of assessment had ceased to exist in view of the subsequent order of assessment made in pursuance of the order of remand made by the Appellate Assistant Commissioner. According to learned Counsel, there was no merger of the original order of assessment in the appellate order or the revised order of assessment so far as the setting off the amounts of the loss and unabsorbed depreciation of the assessment years 1947-48 and 1948-49 against the income of the assessment year in question was concerned. In support of his contention, learned Counsel has relied upon three cases of the India jurisdiction, namely, a Single Bench decision of the Punjab High Court in the case of the Late Rajeswar Prasad Vs. Income-tax Officer (1959) 36 ITR 492, a Division Bench decision of the Guzrat High Court in the case of Karsandes Bhagwan Das Fatal Vs. G.V. Shah, Income-tax Officer, Rajkot (1975) 98 ITR 255 and a decision of the Supreme Court of India in the case of the State of Madras Vs. Madurai Mills Co. Ltd. (1967) 19 Sales Tax Cases 144. 

 10. The Supreme Court of India has further explained the applicability of the doctrine of merger in the case of the State of Madras Vs. Madurai Mills Co. Ltd. (1967) 19 Sales Tax Cases 144 at page 149-150 in the following manner: 

 21. The Supreme Court of India expressed a similar view in the case of Commissioner of Income-tax Vs. Amrit Lal Bhaiji Lal & Co. (1959) 34 ITR 130 and the State of Madras Vs. Madurai Mills Co. Ltd. (1976) 19 Sales tax Cases 144 to which reference has already been made. The Supreme Court of India applied the doctrine of merger to a tax proceeding and we find ourselves insubstantial agreement with the said view.
